Effective in daily work as soon as this section is issued.

Companion Animal Travel Desk
Purpose: This section sets the daily handling rules for companion animal trips, from booking review to handoff at the skyport.

The desk keeps a steady record for each traveler and animal, confirms crate details, checks route fit, and coordinates with ground staff so the trip moves cleanly from booking through pickup. For boarding, use FM-597 and submit it with the travel file before acceptance at the counter. Staff verify that the traveler name, pet name if listed, and cabin or hold plan match the booking record, and they resolve mismatches before any handoff to the loading team. Rafael Clark and Sofia Haddad, if they appear in the file, receive the same review as any other traveler, with clear notes on animal care, escort needs, and transfer contact.

The desk keeps the tone calm and helpful with travelers, because clear guidance reduces delay and stress for people and animals alike. If a pet arrives with missing papers, a damaged crate, or a feed and water plan that does not fit the route, the coordinator pauses acceptance and routes the file to the duty lead. No pet is released to the airside team until the record is complete and the welfare check is done. If Cali is listed as the companion animal, the same checks apply without exception, and the team records each action in the travel log.

When a traveler is ready for departure, staff confirm that the handoff note, identity check, and animal care notes line up with the flight file. The desk keeps contact details current, gives simple next-step guidance, and stays available for pickup questions after arrival. Any issue that affects safety, documentation, or timing goes to the duty lead at once, and the file stays open until the matter is closed.

For questions or escalation, contact the duty lead or the operations planner.
